To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) n-grams are a suitable representation for web intrusion detection, (2) anomaly detection is the more suitable scheme for client-side attacks, while classification should be used for service-side attacks, and (3) n-grams provide a good tradeoff between detection rate and false positive rate for both schemes.

(i) n-gram models are more effective for anomaly detection if they are trained on data with a high degree of diversity and (ii) n-gram classifiers are more effective if they are trained with data that is more homogeneous.

(i) anomaly detection is a more suitable approach for data that has a high degree of diversity and a low level of similarity between instances; (ii) classification is preferable if data is highly repetitive and has a low degree of diversity; and (iii) a hybrid of both approaches is most suitable for data that is repetitive but also contains a high degree of variety.

the question: what is the difference between anomaly detection and classification when applied to n-gram models?
